appraisal_events.evidence: "je n'eus qu'à me rappeler qu'elle ne m'avait pas même offert d'aller voir les Elstir"; "je savais que je ne lui plaisais pas, que je n'avais pas à espérer me faire aimer d'elle".
appraisal_events.explanation: Against Saint-Loup's relayed claim that his aunt feels shunned, the narrator recalls that she never even offered him the visit to see her Elstirs; the invitation is withheld and he leaves for Balbec without her regard, though he forestalls disappointment by disclaiming any expectation.

appraisal_events.evidence: "À tous moments Mme de Marsantes s'interrompait de causer avec Robert pour me dire combien il lui avait souvent parlé de moi, combien il m'aimait ; elle était avec moi d'un empressement... dicté par la crainte qu'elle avait de faire fâcher ce fils... sur lequel elle croyait donc que l'empire qu'elle exerçait n'égalait pas et devait ménager le mien."
appraisal_events.explanation: A marquise courts the narrator with flattering attentions, and the narration makes plain that she does so because she believes his hold on her son greater than her own and dares not cross him.

appraisal_events.evidence: "une sorte de colère semblait s'être élevée en lui, affleurant à son visage durci et sombre. Je craignais qu'au souvenir de la scène de l'après-midi il ne fût humilié vis-à-vis de moi de s'être laissé traiter si durement par sa maîtresse, sans riposter."
appraisal_events.explanation: Robert's anger surfaces visibly, and the narration ties it to the afternoon's scene in which he took his mistress's harshness without answering back, before a witness.

status_effects.explanation: The offered entry into the duchess's house to see the Elstirs never comes, and he departs for Balbec left outside her favour.
He holds the leverage in the room: Robert's mother handles him carefully because she believes his influence over her son exceeds hers.
She is the one who needs, waiting impatiently to have her son to herself and flattering his friend out of fear of displeasing him.
His visible anger and the memory of submitting to his mistress's harshness leave him the humiliated party in front of his friend.

ambiguities: Robert's humiliation is given as the narrator's fear ("je craignais qu'... il ne fût humilié") rather than as an established state; only the anger on his face is directly observed.
